This is the second order model:

second.order.model <- '
# first order model

perf =~ sim + comp + pcomp + parr + bd + oa + cd + mz

I want to fit a model so that everything is constrained but the second-order mean and variance. The second-order variance is released using the group.partial argument, but not the second-order mean

second.2a.fit <- cfa(second.order.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.mean=combined.mean,sample.nobs=combined.n, group.equal=c("loadings", "residuals","lv.variances", "intercepts","means"),group.partial=c("g~~g", "g~1"))

When I re-speficy the model to include the constraints on the first-order means, however, it works as expected.

second.2.order.model <- '
# first order model
verb =~ info + sim + arith + vocab + comp + pcomp + parr
perf =~ sim + comp + pcomp + parr + bd + oa + cd + mz
mem =~ info + arith + ds + ts + bd + cd + mz
# second order model
g=~ verb + perf + mem
# constrain first order factor means to be zero
verb~0*1
perf~0*1
mem~0*1
'

second.2b.fit <- cfa(second.2.order.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.mean=combined.mean,sample.nobs=combined.n,group.equal=c("loadings", "residuals","lv.variances", "intercepts"),group.partial=c("g~~g"))

Am I missing something, or is this a bug?

Best,

Alex

> second-order mean and variance. The second-order variance is released

>
> second.2a.fit <- cfa(second.order.model, sample.cov=combined.cov,
> sample.mean=combined.mean,sample.nobs=combined.n,
> group.equal=c("loadings", "residuals","lv.variances",
> "intercepts","means"),group.partial=c("g~~g", "g~1"))

As a (late) follow-up: this is not so much a bug, it is a limitation of
the group.equal (and group.partial) arguments. They were not designed
with second-order factor models in mind.

The logic is as follows:

1) determine the free parameters in all groups
1b) if we fix the loadings + intercepts, we can also estimate the latent
means in all but the first group
1c) if we also force the latent means to be the same (group.equal
includes "means"), fix all latent means/intercepts to zero
2) which (free!) parameters are constrained to be equal across groups
(loadings, variances, ...)
3) use group.partial to override (otherwise free) parameters that were
constrained to be equal across groups

Because of 1c), the group.partial argument has no (longer) any effect on
the latent intercepts/means, because they are not recognized any longer
as free parameters.

The only way out (for now, 0.5-17) is to use the syntax, perhaps as follows:

fit <- cfa(c(second.order.model, 'verb + perf + mem ~ c(0,0)*1'),
